newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks surge to fresh highs, seen top-heavy.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks surge to fresh highs, seen top-heavy.

text.p: Madrid stocks surged to hit fresh highs at the close on Tuesday, fuelled by an apparently unstoppage wave of domestic buying which made dealers loathe to forecast any ceiling.
But stocks needed to consolidate, they said.
The general index rose 7.03 points, 1.23 percent, to 577.76 and the Ibex-35 gained 93.23 points, 1.42 percent, to 6,675.46.

Santander rose 200 pesetas to 12,750 after news of the purchase of a majority stake in an Argentine bank for 594 million dollars. Bankinter shed 80 pesetas to 25,920 after announcing a three for one share split.
Telefonica soared 95 pesetas in heavy trade to 4,520, bolstered by foreign buying this afternoon.
Gas Natural gained 920 pesetas to 29,800 after news of a four for one share split.
"There's no unexpected bad news from home or from abroad which would prompt anyone to sell, the prospects for a correction don't worry anyone," said a fund manager.
Volume was high again, with a particular amount concentrated in Telefonica amid talk of institutional position-taking.
